instantiate.title: InstantiateMsg
instantiate.description: Instantiation parameters for the wrapper contract.

lock_denom.description: The native/IBC/tokenfactory denom to be locked. Examples: - "ibc/F1073E5895A25347EF10A7B50783D3048882726895AEE1176C498C45D0576F2B" - "coin.zig13g54j2l7039e0py7fr8ekfesqzfd82hdwef3837zzaj9mptq3e7skt4xdr.oro" - "uzig"

mint_decimals.description: Number of decimals for the minted token. Must match the `lock_denom`'s decimals so wallets display 1:1 wrapping correctly. Required — no default, since silently assuming 6 would mis-state precision for any non-stable source token (e.g. 18-decimal ERC-20s).

mint_description.description: Free-form description for the minted token's on-chain metadata. Falls back to "Oroswap <subdenom> Token" if not provided.

mint_max_supply.description:
Wrapper-enforced cap on the circulating supply of the minted denom, expressed in **base units** (i.e. already scaled by `mint_decimals`).

Set this to the source asset's known maximum supply in base units — e.g. for an asset with 6 decimals and a 790,000,000-token max, `mint_max_supply = 790_000_000_000_000`. The contract validates `> 0` at instantiate; consistency with `mint_decimals` is an operator concern. The value is stored in `Config.max_supply` and is immutable after instantiate, so it must be set correctly here.

mint_name.description: Human-readable name for the minted token (e.g. "Wrapped ORO"). Falls back to "Oroswap <subdenom>" if not provided.

mint_subdenom.description: Sub-denom suffix used when creating the ZigChain factory token. The resulting full denom will be: "coin.<contract_address>.<mint_subdenom>" Example: "oro"

mint_symbol.description: Ticker symbol for the minted token (e.g. "xORO"). Falls back to `mint_subdenom` if not provided.

mint_uri.description: Optional URI for the minted token's on-chain metadata.

mint_uri_hash.description: Optional hash of the content addressed by `mint_uri` (e.g. an IPFS CID or sha256 of the logo / manifest). Empty by default. Editable post-instantiate via `UpdateDenomMetadata` since v5 leaves uri_hash on the mutable side of the freeze.

owner.description: Owner / admin of the contract (can pause/unpause and update config).

execute.title: ExecuteMsg
execute.description: Execute messages for the wrapper contract.

oneOf.description: Lock `lock_denom` tokens and receive an equal amount of `mint_denom` tokens. Send native funds with this call. If `receiver` is None the minted tokens go to the sender.
Burn `mint_denom` tokens and receive an equal amount of `lock_denom` tokens back. Send mint tokens as native funds with this call. If `receiver` is None the unlocked tokens go to the sender.
Pause all lock/unlock operations. Callable by the owner or any address in the pause-authority set.
Resume lock/unlock operations. Owner only — a compromised pause authority cannot toggle the pause state on its own.
Proposes a new owner. The proposed owner must call ClaimOwnership within expires_in seconds. Only callable by the current owner.
Removes the pending ownership proposal. Only callable by the current owner.
Claims a pending ownership proposal. Only callable by the proposed new owner.
Recovers any `lock_denom` tokens that were sent directly to the contract without minting, restoring the 1:1 invariant between locked tokens and minted supply. Owner only.

Update the on-chain Metadata of the minted denom. Owner only. True patch semantics: any field left as `None` keeps the value currently stored on-chain; only `Some(_)` fields are overwritten. (The tokenfactory module rewrites Metadata as a whole, so the contract keeps an authoritative copy in storage and re-encodes the full Metadata on every call — never silently regenerating defaults.)

Only `description`, `uri` and `uri_hash` are accepted. The identity fields `name`, `symbol`, `display` and `denom_units` are permanently frozen by the ZIGchain v5 tokenfactory upgrade once `total_minted > 0` (which is always true after the first Lock), so this variant deliberately does not expose them. They are set once at instantiate from the InstantiateMsg fields and never mutated afterwards.

Begin the two-step transfer of the minted denom's bank- and metadata-admin roles to new addresses. The new admins must follow up with a `MsgClaimDenomAdmin` on the chain themselves. Owner only.

Used when retiring this wrapper: the bank_admin gates mint/burn, so the successor contract / multisig must claim before users can keep locking/unlocking.
Add addresses with pause authority. Owner only.
Remove addresses from the pause-authority set. Owner only.

query.title: QueryMsg
query.description: Query messages for the wrapper contract.

oneOf.description: Returns the total amount of `lock_denom` currently held (locked) in the contract. NOTE: If users send `lock_denom` directly to the contract via a standard bank send, this value will encompass that excess. To check the true 1:1 backed invariant, compare this with `MintSupply`.
Returns the total circulating supply of the `mint_denom`.
Returns the list of addresses currently in the pause-authority set. The owner always has implicit pause authority and is NOT included.

migrate.title: MigrateMsg
migrate.description: Message used to trigger a contract migration.

lock_denom.description: The token to be locked — can be any native denom: plain native (e.g. "uzig"), IBC (e.g. "ibc/F1073E..."), or a tokenfactory coin (e.g. "coin.xxx.yyy")

max_supply.description:
Wrapper-enforced cap on the **circulating supply** of the minted denom (in base units). `execute_lock` rejects any mint where `current_supply + mint_amount > max_supply`.

The check is wrapper-side rather than pure tokenfactory because ZigChain's tokenfactory `minting_cap` is enforced against the cumulative `total_minted` counter (not decremented by burns), which would couple the cap to lifetime throughput rather than peak circulating supply. Tracking circulating supply at the wrapper level lets burns free up headroom so the cap applies to instantaneous outstanding supply, matching the intended invariant ("wrapped supply cannot exceed source supply").

mint_decimals.description: Decimal precision of the minted denom, baked in once at `MsgCreateDenom` time. Persisted so `UpdateDenomMetadata` can echo the correct exponent — the chain's Metadata stores DenomUnits, not a free-standing decimals field, and rewriting them with the wrong exponent would mis-state precision in every wallet/explorer.

mint_denom.description: The tokenfactory token minted 1:1 for each locked token (e.g. "coin.<contract_address>.<mint_subdenom>"). Set to "" initially and populated in the reply handler.

paused.description: Whether the contract is currently paused

Addr.description:
A human readable address.

In Cosmos, this is typically bech32 encoded. But for multi-chain smart contracts no assumptions should be made other than being UTF-8 encoded and of reasonable length.

This type represents a validated address. It can be created in the following ways 1. Use `Addr::unchecked(input)` 2. Use `let checked: Addr = deps.api.addr_validate(input)?` 3. Use `let checked: Addr = deps.api.addr_humanize(canonical_addr)?` 4. Deserialize from JSON. This must only be done from JSON that was validated before such as a contract's state. `Addr` must not be used in messages sent by the user because this would result in unvalidated instances.

This type is immutable. If you really need to mutate it (Really? Are you sure?), create a mutable copy using `let mut mutable = Addr::to_string()` and operate on that `String` instance.
